newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore Port Authority wins China terminal deal.
newsitem.headline: Singapore Port Authority wins China terminal deal.

text.p: The Port of Singapore Authority (PSA) said on Monday it won a 50-year deal to manage and operate existing Chinese container terminals and to build a new deep water facility in the southern Chinese port of Fuzhou.
PSA said in a statement it signed a contract on Friday with the Fuzhou Port Authority (FSA) to form joint venture companies to manage the existing terminals at Qingzhou and Daijiang.
Its investment will be through subsidiary Sealion Huanan Pte Ltd and two Hong Kong-based joint venture partners, Ranki Development Ltd and Pacific Industries and Development Ltd.

PSA said its consortium would take a 49-percent stake in the project while FSA the remaining 51-percent. PSA holds a 70-percent stake in the consortium while its Hong Kong partners each have 15 percent.
Pacific Industries and Development Ltd belongs to Indonesian tycoon Liem Sioe Liong of the Salim Group.
PSA declined to say who owned Ranki Development, but Singapore's Business Times newspaper said it was believed to belong to the Henderson Group, a Hong Kong property company..

PSA declined to say how much it would invest in the project, its second port venture in China after the Dalian Container Terminal in NorthEast China, a flagship international port project lauched last year.

Fuzhou's cargo volume grew to 12.47 million tonnes in 1996 from 2.09 million in 1980 while container throughput grew sixfold over the past six years to 177,000 20-ft equivalent units (TEUs) in 1996, PSA said.
Container throughput in Fuzhou is projected to 500,000 by 2000, it said.
